design.element_count_basis: Counted from the transcribed surface table: a run of surfaces that carry an index is one cemented group, and a change of index inside a run starts another element.

aperture_validity.basis: The stop row is an opaque plate whose opening is narrower than the neighbouring elements.
aperture_validity.satisfaction_basis: No field-dependent MTF, relative-illumination or pupil measurement is recorded for this record, so a stop-dependent match is not claimed.

spectrum.sampling_wavelengths_basis: The publication prints the d-line as its reference wavelength. That value is an air wavelength at 20 C and 101325 Pa; the record keeps it as printed and uses the same value in the Project.

band_nm.basis: MODELLING_CONVENTION: the publication states a reference wavelength but no design band, so the model glasses are fitted over the visible band 400-700 nm and no wider validity is claimed.

continuous_coverage_nm.note: The publication states a single reference wavelength, not a specified band.

image_format.basis: DERIVED from the traced chief-ray image height at the stated half field; the publication prints an image height of 21.64 mm, which is the full-frame half diagonal.

materials.basis: Each glass is modelled from the printed nd and Abbe number: a two-term Cauchy curve through (nd, Vd), then a three-term Sellmeier with fixed poles fitted to it over the stated band. The model index is scaled by 1.0002772, the engine's air index at the d line, so that the index ratio at a glass-air surface is the printed nd.

approximations.description: The publication states nd and Vd only. A two-term Cauchy curve is solved exactly from those two values and a three-term Sellmeier with fixed poles is fitted to it. The relative index at the reference wavelength is the source's nd; the dispersion curve is a model.

The semi-diameters in the Project are derived, not transcribed: each is the larger of the paraxial marginal and chief-ray heights at the stated f-number and half field with a 6 % mechanical allowance; the allowance was reduced until neighbouring surfaces no longer meet, so it is the largest value the prescription admits. No clear-aperture value is taken from the publication.

The engine treats a model glass as an absolute refractive index and a gap as air at 20 C and 101325 Pa (n = 1.0002772 at the d line), so the ratio it uses at a glass-air surface is nd / 1.0002772. The model glasses are fitted to nd * 1.0002772 to make that ratio the printed nd. Without the factor the paraxial focal length of the same table is 0.03 % to 0.4 % long, which is a property of the model, not of the transcription.
The publication states the f-number but not the stop diameter. The modelled stop opening is solved so that the paraxial marginal ray reproduces the printed f-number.

validation.paraxial_scope: effective focal length only; no back focal length is transcribed
evidence_notes: Engine paraxial EFL 73.002069 mm against the source's printed 73.0 mm.
Traced chief ray at the stated half field lands at 21.2153 mm against the printed image height 21.64 mm.
